originality.rationale: The full arbitrary-finite-abelian fixed-point distribution, weighted-matchings factorization by the image of A[2] in A/2A, and 2-rank independence of the total count were not found in the inspected sources. This is a nontrivial arithmetic evaluation of the prior comprehensive displacement-map parametrization, not a claimed new classification of possible maps. Taniguchi covers connected quandles; Kamada–Oshiro the cyclic count; Ta gives broader map characterizations and a matching sum for a different cyclic Alexander family. Residual possibility of equivalent enumerations is disclosed.
residual_risks: Theorem 4.2 already parametrizes these maps; the distinction in originality is the evaluated group-uniform distribution, not a new abstract parametrization.
An unindexed equivalent closed evaluation may exist, especially as a specialization of an all-Alexander counting method.

value.rationale: Counts and fixed-point strata of good involutions are natural structural invariants of symmetric quandle enhancements with knot-theoretic motivation. Provides an exact infinite-family enumeration depending only on binary ranks d,e for total counts and |2A| for the fixed-point polynomial. Groups of different sizes and exponents can share the count, while the polynomial distinguishes fixed-point behavior. Not a renamed textbook count or small numerical census; classical matching numbers are used as a tool rather than presented as the novelty.
